summary.prose: This Story makes the daemon's stores and shared state safe to use from several threads before any work moves off the main thread. It proves, per store, how each behaves when a worker thread opens, uses and releases it, and guards any store that is not safe with a process-wide semaphore that is always released. It moves the four MCP step-state stores, the status board and the worker registry into one main-thread hub that every thread reaches by message, so state outlives any worker.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Alternative a1: a routing main thread plus worker threads by class of work. The main thread owns the Unix socket, framing and the attached-client registry, and does no handler work. Each request is classified (admin, session or indexing) and forwarded over a thread channel to its target: the admin worker, the indexing worker, or the session's pooled worker (session id = the request's client label and process id). Workers each load the handler runtime and open their own store handles under a verified per-store threading policy: direct use where a store is proven safe, a shared semaphore with guaranteed release where it is not. MCP step state (the four step state stores) moves into a store shared by all threads, so it outlives any worker; a detached workflow run stays owned by the worker that started it, which is not released while the run is active, and the run's record is published where every thread can read it. A request that carries no valid client identity is served on one shared unattributed worker, as today's daemon serves it, kept apart from every session. A shared status board lets every thread publish what it is doing, which the admin worker reads for daemon status and liveness.

ownedContracts.name: Store guard and per-store threading policy
ownedContracts.purpose: Lets any thread use a store safely: records, per store, whether it is used directly or through a semaphore, and gives one helper that acquires and always releases the store's semaphore. Waiting for a lock is always asynchronous, so a waiting thread keeps serving its other work.

ownedContracts.name: Shared step-state store
ownedContracts.purpose: Keeps MCP step tokens where every thread can read them, so a session served by a new worker after an idle release, or after its worker failed, resumes its step exactly as today. Each of the four step kinds keeps its own lifecycle through an adapter: a 100-entry least-recently-used cap, a read that refreshes the token's expiry, a 1-hour idle TTL, analyze and workflow updates that mint a new token and release the old one, review updates that keep the same token, and code-review transitions that consume the current token and mint a new one at each stage (wait → judgement, fallback), so a superseded token fails exactly as today.

ownedContracts.name: Thread channel and target registry
ownedContracts.purpose: The one message contract between the router and every worker: request, reply, stream frame, cancel and error envelopes, plus the registry where a worker registers as the target for a class of work. A session-class request with no valid session id resolves to the unattributed target.

ownedContracts.name: Thread status board
ownedContracts.purpose: Shared record each thread updates as it starts and finishes work: the router publishes its attached-client snapshot, the indexing worker publishes lane state, summary-sweep progress, each repository's completeness and the unattributed-entity count, and detached workflow runs publish their full poll state, so the admin thread can answer status, debug-status, liveness and run polls without calling into a busy thread or touching a store.

boundary.internal: Verifying each store from several threads of one process (the LMDB graph environment, every Lance table, the in-memory DuckDB pool), including that a worker opening and later releasing its handles does not close a descriptor the process's locks depend on; the semaphore implementation over process-wide shared memory and its holder record; moving the four in-memory step state stores onto the shared step-state store with today's TTL; the status board's attached-client, sweep-progress and run-record slots; the thread channel's serialisation and the target registry's bookkeeping; the status board's shared-memory layout. As the root Story it owns every cross-cutting contract the other Stories consume. Validation: ac1 — one thread writes a repo's entities while another reads the same graph, the reader sees only whole transactions, and an entity's vectors are written only after its graph commit; ac2 — two threads write different artifacts or config entries and a third thread reads both back; ac3 — no code path outside the daemon opens a store; ac4 — a throwing LMDB transaction on one thread leaves nothing visible to another. Also: a worker opening and releasing its handles keeps the process's LMDB locks; the guard releases on success, throw, cancel and worker kill; an acquisition past its limit fails; nested acquisition is refused. Step-state compatibility: for each of the four kinds, token rotation (analyze, workflow), stable-token update (review) or consume-and-mint per stage (code-review, where a superseded token fails), read refresh of expiry, the 100-entry eviction and a missing-token error behave as today. LMDB is opened once per process and never closed by a worker; lock reclaim waits for a dead worker's in-flight native calls. Per store, a quiescence observation with a time limit and an unhealthy-store outcome when it is exceeded; a guard wait never blocks its thread.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The main-thread router (connection handling, classification, envelope forwarding, writing replies and frames back, observing worker exits, reclaiming a dead worker's store locks, coordinating shutdown and the locks-lost path), starting and supervising the admin worker, and classifying all 189 methods. Until a class's target is registered (before s3 or s4 lands) the router serves that class on a fallback worker, so each Story can ship alone. Validation: ac1 and ac2 — ping and daemon.status answer within 100 ms while a session worker spins the CPU and while an indexing pass runs, including while another worker holds the graph guard; ac3 — each admin method's response matches today's recorded response; ac4 — a test enumerates every served RPC and stream method and fails on any without a class, and a dispatch test sends each admin-class method and asserts it ran on the admin thread. Also: debug-status keeps every field including lastMethod; daemon.status and repo.list read only the status board and keep today's full response shapes (RegisteredRepo records, the unattributed count with reasons); contention tests show ping, daemon.status, repo.list and the TUI's other admin reads answer within 100 ms while an indexing pass runs and another worker holds the graph guard, including while repo.stats waits on the guard on the admin worker; shutdown and the locks-lost path behave as today.

Hosting the index queue, both lanes and the file-watcher feed in one indexing worker that registers as the indexing-class target, keeping today's lane ordering and summary-lane yielding, and publishing lane state, idleness, summary-sweep progress, the full registered-repository records with each repository's completeness, and the unattributed-entity count with its reasons, on the status board after every change. Validation: ac1 — a session request is answered during an indexing pass; ac2 — a file change is indexed while a session worker is busy; ac3 — lane order and indexed results equal the single-thread baseline for the same input; ac4 — queue status and idle waiting read from another thread reflect the indexing worker's real state.

The session pool: session-id mapping, per-session FIFO, worker creation and idle release, containment of a failing worker (its in-flight requests fail with an error, the next request gets a new worker), routing each step handler's state through the shared step-state store, the unattributed worker, inline nested calls, and ownership of detached workflow runs (records on the status board, abort routed to the owner, failure on owner exit, never idle-released while a run is active). Validation: ac1 — session B is answered while session A's worker spins; ac2 — A's second request starts only after its first completes; ac3 — requests from one client process over separate connections run on one worker, released after the idle timeout; ac4 — a worker failure fails only its session's requests; ac5 — provider calls stay serial (no Promise.all reaching a provider); ac6 — a step token minted before an idle release resumes on the new worker. Also: unattributed requests are served apart from sessions; a nested in-daemon call completes without deadlock; a detached run survives idle time, accepts an abort from another thread, and is marked failed when its owner exits; a poll from another thread, and after the owner has gone, returns the same frames-since-cursor, model, result and error as today.

Adding a `threads` section to daemon.status and daemon.debug-status from the status board and session pool (additive fields only), and making the liveness answer report a busy session as busy rather than as a failure. Validation: ac1 — daemon.status lists each thread with class, session, busy state, method and elapsed time; ac2 — with a session worker busy for minutes the liveness answer reports the daemon alive and the session busy; ac3 — every field of today's daemon.status and daemon.debug-status, including clients and sweep progress, is present with the same meaning.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase A — store safety and shared contracts

nonFunctional.performance: Ping and daemon.status answer within 100 ms at the 99th percentile while a session worker is CPU-bound and while an indexing pass runs; routing adds no more than 5 ms per request and per stream frame. A session worker's idle timeout defaults to 15 minutes and is configurable; step state keeps its own 1-hour TTL independent of worker release.
nonFunctional.security: No new listener or socket: the main thread keeps the existing Unix socket and its permissions; shared memory and thread channels are internal to the daemon process; clients still reach the stores only through IPC.
nonFunctional.observability: Every log line carries its thread id and class, and the session id for session work; daemon.status lists every thread with class, session, busy state, current method and elapsed time; a store-lock wait beyond its acquisition limit and a reclaimed lock after a worker exit are logged as warnings.
nonFunctional.durability: Step state survives a worker's release or failure because it lives in the shared step-state store; a detached workflow run lives in its owning worker, which is not released while the run is active, and is marked failed if that worker exits; its poll state lives in shared run storage, so polls still answer after the owner has gone. A worker that exits while holding a store lock has the lock reclaimed by the router. Atomicity is unchanged from today: each LMDB write transaction commits all or nothing, and an operation that writes LMDB then Lance keeps today's order and re-embed recovery. The LMDB environment is opened once per process and closed only by the router at shutdown; a lock held by a dead worker is reclaimed only after its in-flight native calls have finished.

api.name: withStore
api.signature: <T>(store: StoreId, op: () => Promise<T>, opts: StoreGuardOptions) => Promise<T>

parameters.name: op
parameters.purpose: The whole guarded operation; the lock is held until it settles, across its awaits.

parameters.name: opts
parameters.purpose: Acquisition time limit and optional abort signal.

returns.meaning: The operation's result; for a direct-mode store the operation runs with no lock.

errors.condition: The permit was not obtained within acquireTimeoutMs.

The same async call chain already holds a permit on any store (withStore called from inside another withStore's op), detected with an async-context marker set for the duration of op; other concurrent requests on the same thread are not nested and wait their turn instead.
opts.signal fired while waiting; nothing was acquired.
The store was marked unhealthy by a failed reclaim.

preconditions: The calling thread was started with the process's shared guard block.
postconditions: Whatever op does (resolve, reject or throw synchronously), the permit is released before the returned promise settles.
The holder record for this thread and store is cleared on release.
Waiting never blocks the thread: other work on the thread keeps running while it waits.

Concurrent calls from different async call chains on the same thread queue in arrival order for the store's permit and each runs when it obtains one; only a call made from inside a held op is refused as nested.
Holders are recorded per acquisition (acquisition id, thread id, store, acquired-at), not one slot per thread, so one thread can have several queued or running acquisitions over time.

api.name: reclaim
api.signature: (threadId: number) => Promise<{ readonly released: readonly StoreId[]; readonly unhealthy: readonly StoreId[] }>

returns.meaning: Stores whose permits the dead worker held and that were released, and stores that did not quiesce within their limit and are now unhealthy.

preconditions: Called on the main thread after the worker's 'exit' event.
postconditions: A permit is released only after the store's quiescence check confirms the dead worker's native calls have finished.
A store that does not quiesce within limitMs is marked unhealthy, every later withStore on it fails, and the caller is expected to restart the daemon.

api.name: mint

errors.condition: The payload holds a value structured clone cannot carry.

postconditions: Expired entries (touched more than ttlMs ago) are swept first and the least recently touched are evicted while the kind holds maxEntries, as the four stores do today.

api.name: read

returns.meaning: The entry, or undefined when the token is unknown, expired or superseded; callers keep raising today's kind-specific not-found errors.

postconditions: A found entry's touchedAt is refreshed, as today's loadState does.

api.name: update
api.signature: (kind: StepKind, token: string, payload: P) => Promise

parameters.name: kind
parameters.purpose: Which step store; its lifecycle decides the token rule.

returns.meaning: The token to use next: the same token for review (stable-token), a new token for analyze and workflow (rotate-token, the old one released), and a new token for code-review stage transitions (consume-per-stage).

postconditions: For rotate-token and consume-per-stage kinds the old token reads as undefined afterwards.

api.name: release

returns.meaning: The entry is gone; releasing an unknown token is a no-op, as today.

postconditions: read(kind, token) returns undefined.

parameters.name: session
parameters.purpose: Validated session identity; absent for admin, indexing and unattributed requests.

returns.meaning: The registered target, the unattributed target for a session-class request without identity, or undefined when nothing is registered (the router's fallback then applies).

parameters.name: target
parameters.purpose: A worker announcing what it serves.

returns.meaning: The target is resolvable by targetFor.

api.name: unregister

parameters.name: threadId
parameters.purpose: The worker that exited, was released or was replaced.

returns.meaning: Every target that thread registered is removed; targetFor no longer returns it.

api.name: publish

returns.meaning: Fire-and-forget from a worker (one ordered message); the board keeps the latest status per thread.

postconditions: snapshot() reflects the newest status from each thread in the order each thread sent them.

parameters.name: status
parameters.purpose: Lane depths, processing flags, sweep progress and idleness from the indexing thread.

returns.meaning: One ordered fire-and-forget message; the board keeps the latest.

postconditions: snapshot().indexing equals the last value sent.

parameters.name: clients
parameters.purpose: The router's attached-client registry in today's shape, lastMethod included.

preconditions: Sent by the router (main thread) after each registry change.
postconditions: snapshot().clients equals the last list sent, field for field.

api.name: publishRun

parameters.name: run
parameters.purpose: A detached workflow run's full poll state.

returns.meaning: Inserts or replaces the record with that runId.

preconditions: Sent by the worker that owns the run, after each frame and at completion.
postconditions: snapshot().runs holds the latest record per runId; frames only grow.

api.name: publishStore

parameters.name: store
parameters.purpose: Registered repositories with completeness and the unattributed count, in today's shapes.

preconditions: Sent by the indexing thread after each change to those values.
postconditions: snapshot().store equals the last value sent; before the first send its fields are undefined.

api.name: snapshot

returns.meaning: Threads, indexing state, clients, runs and the store snapshot as last published; a worker obtains it with one async hub request.

postconditions: Never touches a store and never waits on a store lock.

api.name: getLanceConn

returns.meaning: This thread's Lance connection, opened with readConsistencyInterval 0 so every read sees writes committed by any thread.

errors.condition: The live path is opened by a thread of a process that has not declared itself the store owner.

postconditions: A table handle opened from this connection sees another thread's committed writes on its next read.

api.name: declareLiveStoreOwner

returns.meaning: Marks this thread's module instance as belonging to the store-owning daemon process.

preconditions: Called by the daemon's main thread at start, and by every daemon worker at start (the flag is module-scope, so each isolate needs it); never by a client process.
postconditions: isLiveStoreOwnerDeclared() is true in that thread.

dataModelChanges.details: One in-memory map per StepKind on the main-thread hub, replacing the four module maps; each kind's StepLifecycle carries maxEntries 100, ttlMs 1 hour, readRefreshes true and its update rule (analyze, workflow: rotate-token; review: stable-token; code-review: consume-per-stage). Lost on daemon restart, as today. Every caller becomes async and gains an await, including the encode/reencode/decode wrappers and their callers (a missed await would hand a Promise to the stage check). The full production call-site list: src/daemon/steps/code-review-step/handler.ts:252, :262, :312, :325, :332, :364, :431, :509, :523, :586; src/daemon/steps/review-step/phases/start.ts:80, :106; src/daemon/steps/review-step/phases/claims.ts:32, :42; src/daemon/steps/review-step/phases/findings.ts:39, :87, :95; src/daemon/steps/review-step/phases/verdicts.ts:41, :89, :101; src/daemon/steps/analyze-step/state.ts:132, :150, :169 (encodeState, reencodeState, decodeState); src/daemon/steps/analyze-step/phases/start.ts:131; src/daemon/steps/analyze-step/phases/plan.ts:68, :173, :232; src/daemon/steps/analyze-step/phases/narrow.ts:64, :252, :305; src/daemon/steps/analyze-step/phases/bundle.ts:66, :132; src/daemon/steps/workflow-step/state.ts:88, :106, :119 (encodeState, reencodeState, decodeState); src/daemon/steps/workflow-step/phases/start.ts:102; src/daemon/steps/workflow-step/phases/plan.ts:36, :82, :105; src/daemon/steps/workflow-step/phases/step.ts:34, :84, :107; src/daemon/steps/workflow-step/phases/synthesize.ts:35, :95. The test-only helpers (_clear…StateStoreForTests, _…StateStoreSize, _stateStoreSize) become async helpers that act on the hub's map for that kind; their 27 test-file users await them (for example src/daemon/__tests__/code-review-rpc-fallback.test.ts, src/workflow/code-review/__tests__/diff-attribution.test.ts, src/workflow/code-review/__tests__/subject-attribution.test.ts, src/daemon/steps/__tests__/analyze-step-state.test.ts, src/daemon/steps/__tests__/peer-state-store-leakfree.test.ts).

One process-wide shared-memory block created by the main thread and passed to each worker at start: per store a permit counter (graph and lance: direct, no permit taken; duckdb: guarded, 1 permit; the graph has no guarded mode, because a per-thread open is exactly what the gate tests, so until the gate passes the graph is opened only by the main thread) and holder records per acquisition (acquisition id, thread id, acquired-at). Holder records let reclaim release every permit a dead worker held. In front of the shared permit each thread keeps a local arrival-order queue, so concurrent async requests on one thread wait their turn rather than conflict. The block also holds the process-wide store health word: 0 = ok, 1 = locks-lost (with the detecting thread id). recordLocksLost sets it with an atomic compare-and-swap (so only the first detection in the process logs) and the detecting thread publishes the full health record (operation, at, detectedBy, libraryMessage) through the hub to every thread, which keeps a copy. Every reader of the health state reads the shared word first: getStoreHealth, recordLocksLost's set-once guard, getGraphStore, withWriteTxn, withWriteTxnSync, runReaderCheck (which then skips its probe) and closeGraphStore (which then skips the library close). Until a thread has received the full record, its LmdbStoreLocksLostError messages and close-skip log name the detecting thread instead of the failed operation.

Main-thread record holding the latest ThreadStatus per thread, IndexingStatus, AttachedClientSnapshot[], RunRecord[] and StoreStatusSnapshot exactly as sc4 defines; written by publish* calls, read by snapshot().
lancedb.connect is called with readConsistencyInterval 0 so cross-thread writes are visible on the next read; writes were already consistent.

Initial table, each entry with its evidence. graph: direct, but only once the gating worker open-and-release test passes; if it fails, s1 records the result, no worker opens LMDB, and the question goes back to the HLD (open question) before s3 or s4 starts, since workers would then have no supported way to reach the graph. lance: direct with strong read consistency. duckdb: guarded with one permit, each thread opening its own in-memory instance behind it, which bounds total memory to one 2 GB budget. 'Guarded' always means each thread opens its own handle and takes the store's permit around every use.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: withStore, policy, holders, reclaim and quiescence over the shared StoreGuardBlock; async wait only; nested acquisition refused per async call chain (async-context marker), concurrent requests on one thread queued in arrival order, holders recorded per acquisition; release in a finally; reclaim waits for per-store quiescence and marks a store unhealthy past limitMs. The block also carries the process-wide store health word that every thread checks before each store call.

The main-thread hub hosts the four step kinds behind SharedStepStateStore with per-kind StepLifecycle adapters; workers use a hub client with the same interface over their channel port; the existing saveState/loadState/replaceState/updateState/releaseState wrappers delegate to it and become async.

Defines the ChannelEnvelope types plus the hub request/reply envelopes used by the step-state and board clients, and the TargetRegistry on the main thread with register, unregister and targetFor; s2 builds the router on top.

StatusBoard lives on the main thread with publish, publishIndexing, publishClients, publishRun, publishStore and snapshot; every publish* from a worker is a one-way ordered message keeping the latest value (runs keyed by runId), snapshot from a worker is one hub request; nothing in it reads a store.

errorCases.scenario: A worker thread opening or releasing the LMDB environment drops the process's POSIX lock on graph.lmdb-lock (the library opens and closes an extra lock-file descriptor on every open).
errorCases.detection: The gating reproduction test: a worker opens the store, reads, closes its handle and exits; then the main thread writes and a second process opens and closes the store; the main thread's next write must succeed. In production the existing lock-loss detection (store health moving to locks-lost on MDB_LOCK_FAILURE or MDB_BAD_RSLOT) still applies.
errorCases.response: If the test passes, graph is direct: every worker opens its own handle and never closes the environment. If it fails, s1 records the result as the graph policy's evidence, no worker opens LMDB, and the question goes back to the HLD (an open question on this LLD) before s3 or s4 starts.
errorCases.userImpact: None if caught by the gate; otherwise the daemon would hit today's locks-lost path.

errorCases.scenario: A guarded operation throws, rejects, or its signal aborts while it holds a permit.
errorCases.detection: withStore wraps the operation in try/finally.
errorCases.response: The permit and holder slot are released in the finally before the error propagates unchanged.
errorCases.userImpact: Only the failing request sees the error.

errorCases.scenario: A thread waits for a permit past acquireTimeoutMs.
errorCases.response: StoreLockTimeoutError naming the store and the current holder (thread id, held since); a warning is logged.
errorCases.userImpact: That request fails with a clear message instead of hanging.

errorCases.scenario: Code running inside a held withStore op calls withStore again (same or different store).
errorCases.detection: An async-context marker (set by withStore for the duration of op and inherited by everything op awaits) is present when withStore is entered.
errorCases.response: StoreLockNestedError, thrown before waiting, so no lock cycle can form; a concurrent request on the same thread that is not inside op carries no marker and simply queues.
errorCases.userImpact: A programming error surfaces in tests rather than as a deadlock.

errorCases.scenario: A worker exits or is terminated while holding a permit.
errorCases.detection: The main thread's worker 'exit' event; holder slots list that thread id.
errorCases.response: reclaim waits for the store's quiescence (no native call from that thread still running, observed per store) up to limitMs, then releases; past the limit the store is marked unhealthy and later withStore calls fail with StoreUnhealthyError.
errorCases.userImpact: Other threads resume once the permit is reclaimed; an unhealthy store needs a daemon restart.

errorCases.scenario: A step payload contains a value structured clone cannot carry.
errorCases.detection: postMessage throws DataCloneError when a worker sends it to the hub.
errorCases.response: The error propagates to the phase handler and the request fails; the per-kind clone test is meant to catch this before release.
errorCases.userImpact: That step call fails instead of silently losing state.

errorCases.scenario: A worker sends a hub request and the main thread never replies (the port closed).
errorCases.detection: The hub client's pending-request map is failed by the port's close event.
errorCases.response: Every pending request rejects with HubUnavailableError.

errorCases.scenario: A client presents a step token that was superseded, released or expired.
errorCases.response: The kind's existing not-found error (StateTokenNotFound, StepStateDecodeError 'not-found', WorkflowStateDecodeError 'not-found') with today's message.

errorCases.scenario: One thread detects lost LMDB locks (MDB_LOCK_FAILURE or MDB_BAD_RSLOT) while other threads still hold the store.
errorCases.detection: recordLocksLost in the detecting thread sets the process-wide health word with a compare-and-swap and publishes the full record through the hub; getStoreHealth, getGraphStore, withWriteTxn, withWriteTxnSync, runReaderCheck and closeGraphStore read the word before acting in every thread.
errorCases.response: Every thread's next store call fails with LmdbStoreLocksLostError (naming the failed operation once the record arrives, the detecting thread before that), runReaderCheck stops probing, closeGraphStore skips the library close, and only the first detection is logged, as today's single-thread path behaves.
errorCases.userImpact: Same as today's locks-lost: the daemon reports the store failure and needs a restart; no thread keeps writing to a store whose locks are gone.

edgeCases.expected: Same token both times; the second read returns the latest payload.

edgeCases.input: An analyze token used after replaceState minted its successor
edgeCases.expected: read returns undefined; the old token fails as today.

edgeCases.input: A code-review confirm_wait token after the run resumed
edgeCases.expected: The wait token reads as undefined; only the newly minted judgement token works.
The least recently touched entry of that kind is evicted, as today; other kinds are unaffected.

edgeCases.input: A token read just before its TTL
edgeCases.expected: The read refreshes touchedAt, so it survives another hour.
The operation runs with no permit taken; holders() is unchanged.

edgeCases.input: Two threads ask for the DuckDB permit at once
edgeCases.expected: One runs; the other waits asynchronously and runs after release, in turn.
Empty threads, idle indexing with zero depths, no clients or runs, and a store snapshot with repos and unattributedUnwritable undefined.

edgeCases.input: A worker publishes several statuses quickly
edgeCases.expected: The board keeps the last one sent, because messages on one port arrive in order.

edgeCases.input: Two concurrent requests on one thread both call withStore('duckdb')
edgeCases.expected: The second waits asynchronously in arrival order and runs when the first releases; neither fails as nested.

invariantsToPreserve.text: An LMDB write is one synchronous transaction; a throwing callback inside withWriteTxn commits nothing (childTransaction), and async callbacks are refused.
Only the declared store-owning daemon process opens the live LMDB and Lance stores; any other process gets the not-owner error.
After locks-lost every store call fails with LmdbStoreLocksLostError and closeGraphStore skips the library close; with several threads this holds in every thread, not only the one that detected it.
Each step kind keeps a 100-entry cap with least-recently-touched eviction, a 1-hour idle TTL, a read that refreshes the expiry, and its own token rule; a daemon restart loses all step state.
Step tokens are 22-character URL-safe random strings.
One process holds one native LMDB environment per path; a second open reuses it by reference count.
Lance writes are always consistent; DuckDB stays in-memory with extensions locked down and its memory limit applied.

migration.stateBefore: One JavaScript thread owns every store: the graph store is a module-scope singleton opened by getGraphStore (src/db/graph/store.ts:528-531), the owner is declared once in main() (src/daemon/index.ts:130), Lance opens one connection with default (unchecked) read consistency (src/db/lance/conn.ts:86), DuckDB is one in-memory instance (src/daemon/db/duckdb-pool.ts:67). The four MCP step stores are synchronous module-scope maps with a 100-entry LRU and 1-hour TTL (src/daemon/steps/code-review-step/state-store.ts:22-100 and siblings), called from about 50 sites. There is no status board or worker registry, and no shared memory.
migration.stateAfter: Still one thread serves every request (s2-s4 move work later), but the shared pieces are ready: a main-thread hub hosts the four step kinds behind one async SharedStepStateStore with per-kind lifecycle adapters, the status board and the target registry, reachable from workers by message; the store guard's shared-memory block and per-store policy exist (graph opened only by the main thread until the worker open-and-release test passes, then direct; Lance direct with readConsistencyInterval 0, DuckDB guarded with one permit); every worker entry declares the store owner. All step-state callers await the async API with unchanged behaviour.

migrationSteps.action: Add the gating integration test: a worker opens, reads and closes the LMDB store while the main thread holds it, then a second process opens and closes it, and the main thread writes again; record the result as the graph policy's evidence.

Add the store guard (shared-memory block with permits, holder slots and the process-wide store health word; withStore, holders, reclaim with per-store quiescence) and the initial per-store policy table; make getGraphStore, withWriteTxn, withWriteTxnSync and closeGraphStore read the shared health word; nothing calls withStore yet.
Open Lance with readConsistencyInterval 0 and add the cross-thread visibility test.
Add the channel envelope types, the hub request/reply protocol, the main-thread TargetRegistry and StatusBoard, and the worker-side hub client.
Add the SharedStepStateStore on the hub with the four lifecycle adapters and the structured-clone test per kind.

Switch the four state-store modules to delegate to the shared store, make their wrappers and the encode/reencode/decode wrappers async, add await at every listed call site in the phase handlers and the code-review handler, and turn the test-only clear/size helpers into async hub-backed helpers awaited by their test users; existing step tests must pass unchanged in meaning.
Make declareLiveStoreOwner part of the worker entry so every daemon thread declares itself, keeping the client-process refusal.

migration.backwardCompat: No IPC method, request or response changes. Step tokens keep their 22-character form, TTL, LRU cap, read refresh, per-kind token rules and not-found messages, and are still lost on a daemon restart; tokens minted before the update are lost by the update's restart, as today. The step-state module functions keep their names but return promises, which only daemon-internal callers use.

alternativesConsidered.name: Main-thread hub over the thread channel, semaphores in shared memory
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The step-state store, status board and target registry live on the main thread and workers reach them with async request/reply messages over the thread channel; the store guard's semaphores and holder records live in one process-wide shared-memory block so a wait is a non-blocking async wait.

alternativesConsidered.name: Everything in shared memory
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Status board, target registry, semaphores and step state all live in SharedArrayBuffer arenas that every thread reads and writes directly with atomic operations.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Partial on sc2 and sc4 because fixed shared-memory arenas impose capacity limits today's state does not have, at the highest cost.

alternativesConsidered.name: LMDB-backed shared state
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Step state, the status board and run records are stored in dedicated LMDB sub-databases that every thread opens through the one process-wide environment.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates sc4: the status board must answer when the store has failed, and it would be stored in the failing store.

alternativesConsidered.name: Session-local cache with write-through to the hub
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Like a1, but each worker keeps a synchronous local cache of its session's step state and writes through to the main-thread hub, fetching on a cache miss.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Same as a1 on everything but sc2, where two coherent copies add risk for a latency gain the design does not need.

openQuestions: If the gating worker open-and-release test fails, workers cannot open LMDB safely and the HLD's per-worker store handles do not hold for the graph; this goes back to the HLD before s3 or s4 starts.

citations.quotedText: Store lifecycle is in src/db/graph/store.ts: LmdbStoreLocksLostError (159), declareLiveStoreOwner (352) / isLiveStoreOwnerDeclared (393), the module-scope health record `_health` (439), getGraphStore (528), closeGraphStore (901) and withWriteTxn (958, callbacks must be synchronous, 967).

Each step state store keeps `const store = new Map<string, Entry>()` with a 22-char random token, MAX_ENTRIES = 100 with LRU eviction on save, TTL_MS = 1 hour swept on save, and a load that refreshes touchedAt.

If None, then consistency is not checked. ... For strong consistency, set this to zero seconds. ... Write operations are always consistent.
let _health: StoreHealth = { state: 'ok' }; ... _health = { state: 'locks-lost', ... } (module-scope, per isolate)
withConnection: a fresh connection per call on the shared instance, with no serialisation
Opening and closing a second descriptor on the lock file inside the daemon drops the daemon's lock on it (Story s4).
